title: Robotics
tagline: Rigid-body motions, forward and inverse kinematics, Jacobians, manipulator dynamics, trajectory planning, motion and force control, mobile robots and motion planning
summary: Robots are mechanisms under computer control. The course describes rigid-body motion with rotation matrices and homogeneous transformations, solves the forward and inverse kinematics of manipulators, derives velocity Jacobians and singularities, formulates manipulator dynamics, plans trajectories, designs joint-space, task-space and force controllers, and introduces mobile robots, perception and motion planning.
overview: Robots are mechanisms under computer control. The course describes rigid-body motion with rotation matrices and homogeneous transformations, solves the forward and inverse kinematics of manipulators, derives velocity Jacobians and singularities, formulates manipulator dynamics, plans trajectories, designs joint-space, task-space and force controllers, and introduces mobile robots, perception and motion planning.

The course begins with the mathematical description of rigid-body motions: rotation matrices, Euler angles, quaternions and homogeneous transformations. These tools are then applied to the forward kinematics of serial manipulators using the Denavit-Hartenberg convention and the product-of-exponentials formula. The inverse kinematics is solved geometrically for simple robots and numerically for general 6-axis manipulators, with attention to multiple solutions, workspace boundaries and singularities.

Velocity kinematics is described by the manipulator Jacobian, which maps joint velocities to end-effector twist and joint torques to end-effector wrenches. The manipulability ellipsoid and Yoshikawa index characterize the robot's velocity and force capabilities. Manipulator dynamics is formulated using the Euler-Lagrange and Newton-Euler approaches, yielding the mass matrix, Coriolis and gravity terms that govern the robot's dynamic behavior.

Trajectory planning generates smooth joint-space and Cartesian-space motion using polynomial, trapezoidal and s-curve profiles. Robot control encompasses joint-space PID, computed-torque feedback linearization, operational-space control, and impedance and hybrid position/force control for contact tasks. The course concludes with mobile robot kinematics, odometry, path-following control, configuration-space motion planning and probabilistic state estimation.

The course emphasizes the geometric and algebraic structures underlying robot kinematics and dynamics, the computational complexity of forward and inverse problems, and the practical implementation of real-time control algorithms on industrial and research platforms.
outcomes: Describe rigid-body motions using rotation matrices, Euler angles, quaternions and homogeneous transformations
Solve the forward kinematics of serial manipulators using the DH convention and the product-of-exponentials formula
Solve the inverse kinematics geometrically and numerically, identifying multiple solutions and singularities
Derive the manipulator Jacobian and analyze singularities, manipulability and static force mapping
Formulate manipulator dynamics using Euler-Lagrange and Newton-Euler methods
Plan joint-space and Cartesian-space trajectories using polynomial, trapezoidal and s-curve profiles
Design joint-space, computed-torque, impedance and hybrid position/force controllers
Analyze mobile robot kinematics, odometry and path-following control
Apply configuration-space motion planning and probabilistic state estimation to autonomous navigation

chapters.title: Rigid-body motions and transformations
chapters.summary: Rotation matrices, Euler angles, quaternions and homogeneous transformations.

chapters.title: Forward kinematics
chapters.summary: Joint variables, Denavit–Hartenberg parameters and the product-of-exponentials formula.

chapters.title: Inverse kinematics
chapters.summary: Analytical and numerical solutions of the inverse kinematics, multiple solutions and workspaces.

chapters.title: Velocity kinematics and Jacobians
chapters.summary: The manipulator Jacobian, singularities, manipulability, and the relation between joint torques and end-effector forces.

chapters.title: Manipulator dynamics
chapters.summary: The Euler–Lagrange and Newton–Euler equations of motion of robot arms.

chapters.title: Trajectory planning
chapters.summary: Point-to-point and path trajectories in joint and task space, polynomial and spline profiles, and time scaling.

chapters.title: Motion and force control
chapters.summary: Independent-joint PID control, computed-torque control, task-space control, and impedance and force control.

chapters.title: Mobile robots
chapters.summary: Kinematics of wheeled robots, odometry, and the basics of localisation and mapping.

chapters.title: Motion planning and perception
chapters.summary: Configuration space, sampling-based motion planners, and sensing for robots with cameras and lidar.

history.title: Cayley's theory of screw displacements
history.detail: Arthur Cayley publishes the theory of screw displacements, which is the mathematical foundation of rigid-body kinematics and the product-of-exponentials formula.

history.title: Denavit-Hartenberg convention
history.detail: Jacques Denavit and Richard-Hartenberg publish their robot kinematics convention, providing a systematic method for describing the forward kinematics of serial manipulators.

history.title: Pieper's closed-form inverse kinematics
history.detail: Donald Pieper's PhD thesis proves that a 6R manipulator with a spherical wrist has a closed-form inverse kinematics solution, enabling real-time control of industrial robots.

history.title: Paul's robot manipulator programming
history.detail: Richard Paul publishes Robot Manipulators: Mathematics, Programming and Control, the first comprehensive textbook on robot kinematics, dynamics and control.

history.title: Yoshikawa's manipulability
history.detail: Tsuneo Yoshikawa introduces the manipulability measure, providing a quantitative index for robot dexterity and singularity analysis.

history.title: Khatib's operational space formulation
history.detail: Oussama Khatib publishes the operational space formulation, unifying motion and force control of robot manipulators in task space.

history.title: PRM probabilistic roadmaps
history.detail: Kavraki, Svestka, Latombe and Overmars publish the Probabilistic Roadmap method, enabling motion planning for high-dimensional robots.

history.title: LaValle's RRT
history.detail: Steven LaValle publishes Rapidly-exploring Random Trees, providing a practical sampling-based motion planner for single-query problems.

history.title: KUKA LBR iiwa collaborative robot
history.detail: KUKA introduces the LBR iiwa, a 7-axis redundant robot with torque sensors in every joint, enabling compliant impedance control for collaborative assembly.
